changelog: Insert a narrow surface check after C5 to forbid cuts that separate a numeral/quantifier from its immediately following measurement or unit phrase, addressing the primary finding about number+unit cohesion.
findings: The prompt underrates cuts that leave a scope-bearing predicate, auxiliary, negation, or quantifier detached from the phrase that supplies its object/complement or resolves its scope; such early cuts create high contradiction risk when the continuation completes or reverses the left piece.
The prompt fails to protect numerals and measurement phrases: it allows cuts that separate a cardinal/measurement from its unit, breaking referent identity and lowering cohesion.

edits.was: - Long noun phrases with postnominal modifiers, prepositional complements, numer
edits.now: - Narrow check: do not cut between a numeral (digits or spelled-out) or quantifi

diagnosis.why: Inserting the narrow check after C5 that forbids cuts between numerals/quantifiers and their immediately following unit/measurement phrases caused the model to stop splitting number+unit sequences (improving the smallest pieces, ≤3), but it also changed cut priorities elsewhere so many mid-length examples (bins ≤5 and ≤10) now get cuts shifted into noun phrases, enumerations, or auxiliary/subject boundaries; the result is a near-zero net change because roughly as many pairs improved as degraded.
diagnosis.lesson: A later revision should keep numeral+unit adjacency (so short pieces benefit) while avoiding wholesale re-prioritization of cut placement that splits enumerations or breaks cohesive noun phrases in the ≤5–≤10 bins.
